overview: Two chromosome-number states describing whether a cell has one or two sets of chromosomes.
genZNote: Haploid: single set, like one shoe. Diploid: the matching pair.

aspects.label: Number of Chromosome Sets
aspects.valueB: Two complete sets of chromosomes, one from each parent (2n).

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Gametes (sperm, egg); many fungi and algae in their main life stage.
aspects.valueB: Most somatic (body) cells in humans and animals.

aspects.label: How It Forms
aspects.valueA: Formed by meiosis, halving the chromosome number.
aspects.valueB: Formed by fertilisation, when two haploid gametes fuse.

overlay.commonMisconception: Not all organisms are diploid for most of their life cycle — many fungi and algae spend most of their life as haploid.
